title: Sampling CPU Profiler
description: A sampling profiler interrupts the program periodically and records the call stack, building a statistical picture of where time goes. Low overhead makes it safe for production. The picture is statistical but honest.

title: Flame Graphs
description: Flame graphs stack sampled call stacks into a visual mountain where width is time. The eye finds the wide plateaus instantly. They turn profiles into insight at a glance.

demo.code:
print("render  [████████████] 42%")
print("io     [████████] 30%")
print("parse  [█████] 18%")
print("plateau = optimize here")

title: Instrumentation Profiler
description: Instrumentation inserts probes at function entry/exit for exact counts and times. Precision costs overhead, sometimes 10x. Use it for small regions, not whole programs.

demo.code:
print("render: called 1,204 times, total 42.0s")
print("overhead: 8x (use on hot regions only)")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Instrumentation', 'target': 'Function times', 'method': 'Entry/exit probes', 'metric': 'Exact times', 'benefit': 'Exact counts', 'complexity': 'Medium'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'target', 'method', 'metric', 'benefit', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Heap Profiling
description: Heap profilers track allocations by call site, revealing where memory comes from. Allocation hotspots often matter more than leaks. The profile shows the garbage before it becomes a problem.

title: GPU Kernel Profiling (Nsight)
description: Nsight profiles GPU kernels with hardware counters: occupancy, memory throughput, compute throughput. The roofline model shows whether kernels are memory or compute bound. Optimization targets the bound.

title: Wall-Clock vs CPU Time
description: Wall-clock includes waiting; CPU time counts only computation. The gap between them is I/O and locks. Profiling both separates compute problems from waiting problems.

demo.code:
wall, cpu = 100.0, 35.0
print("wall: %.0fs cpu: %.0fs -> waiting: %.0fs" % (wall, cpu, wall - cpu))
print("problem: WAITING (not compute)")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Time split', 'target': 'Program time', 'method': 'Dual measurement', 'metric': 'Wall vs CPU', 'benefit': 'Separates wait from work', 'complexity': 'Low'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'target', 'method', 'metric', 'benefit', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

demo.code:

s = sorted(times)
print("p50: %.1f p99: %.1f (outlier excluded by stats)" % (s[3], s[-1]))
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Rigorous bench', 'target': 'Any measurement', 'method': 'Warmup + distribution', 'metric': 'P50/P99', 'benefit': 'Rumor to data', 'complexity': 'Low'}

title: Lock Contention Profiling
description: Contention profilers measure time threads spend waiting on locks, attributing it to the lock and the holders. The fix is usually finer granularity or lock-free structures. Waiting threads are wasted cores.

title: I/O Profiling (strace)
description: System call tracing shows every read, write, and their latencies. Small reads and fsync storms stand out. I/O problems hide in syscalls.

title: Differential Profiling
description: Two profiles are compared to isolate what a change affected: the diff shows only moved time. Optimization claims are verified by the diff. 'Faster' becomes a number.

title: Energy Profiling
